articleTitle: Prototype of Automatic Calibration System Based on IoT for Weights Using Conveyor Scale
abstract: Calibration of weight standards aims to ensure the accuracy and traceability of measurement results. In Indonesia, manual calibration of weight standards is still commonly used, which comes with risks such as the potential for weights to fall during the transfer process, damaging their physical and metrological characteristics. Additionally, large falling weights can injure calibration personnel. This study developed a prototype of an automated Internet of Things (IoT)-based calibration system using a conveyor scale. The prototype follows the calibration method outlined in OIML R 111-1: 2004. The system is equipped with BME280 sensor to read temperature, humidity, and air pressure to monitor environmental conditions. The system automatically records calibration data and environmental conditions to Google Sheets. Accuracy tests confirmed that the BME280 sensor is functioning properly. Reliability tests showed that it provided stable readings over an hour at different points. The conveyor scale can measure weights from 20 to 600 g, with a resolution of 0.1 g and a maximum error of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 1$</tex> g. Linearity tests indicated that the scale readings are very consistent, and repeatability tests showed a standard deviation of 0.4 g. The maximum differences from the eccentricity test were 0.1 g for dynamic measurements and 0.2 g for static measurements.

articleTitle: Video Processing and Monitoring Animal Movement Models to Measure Learning and Memory in the T Maze Spontaneous Alternation Test with YOLO Implementation
abstract: Monitoring the behavior of mice as an animal model is vital in medical research for understanding diseases and testing potential drugs. The T Maze Spontaneous Alternation Test measures learning and memory in mice. This paper proposes a video processing system using YOLOv8 for real-time tracking of mice, aiming to enhance accuracy and efficiency over traditional manual methods. Comparative experiments demonstrate a significant increase in data accuracy and efficiency. Our system achieves an average accuracy of 0.951 with a recall of 0. 981. The system automates behavior analysis in a T maze, offering potential applications in research on neurological disorders and cognitive impairments.

articleTitle: Feasibility Study of SuperSUN Solar Power Plant for Enhanced Electrification and Sustainability in Remote Regions
abstract: Currently, the electricity needs of the Liukang Tupabiring Utara District are met by generators, as there is no conventional electricity grid due to the district's geographically challenging and remote location, consisting of small islands. Establishing a PLN electricity distribution network in this area is considered inefficient. This situation is of particular concern regarding the electrification ratio target in Pangkep Regency, which is set at 100% for 2024, with a realization of 99.78% as of 2023. Indonesia's electricity needs are largely supported by conventional fossil fuel power plants, which are depleting and emitting CO2 pollutants. To increase the electrification ratio in 3T areas (Lagging, Leading, and Outermost) and reduce CO2 emissions, environmentally friendly power plants are needed. This study aims to analyze solar energy utilization using the SuperSUN model by calculating solar energy values, comparing economic investment values, and assessing the feasibility of using the SuperSUN solar power plant in Pangkep Regency. The research method is quantitative, with data collected through field observations covering the local community's electricity needs and meteorological conditions (temperature, sunlight intensity, and wind speed). The modelling was then carried out using PVSyst 7.2 software. The results showed that the total solar energy produced in one year is 1,088.7 kWh, with a Performance Ratio (PR) of 0.381 and a Solar Fraction (SF) of 0.991. Regarding investment, SuperSUN is more efficient than communal solar power plants. Based on the feasibility study, the SuperSUN solar power plant is viable for meeting the electrification ratio target and supporting the Net Zero Emission program.

articleTitle: Error Angle Sun Earth Geometry Analysis on Fuzzy Logic Method in Dual-Axis Solar Tracking Mounting Design
abstract: The distribution of solar radiation in Indonesia reaches 4.8 kWh/m2, this makes Indonesia a potential region for utilizing solar energy as a solar power plant. In general, photovoltaic (PV) modules are built with a statically mounting construction, which results in suboptimal absorption of solar irradiation due to the sun's apparent movement. Therefore, this research aims to develop a dual-axis solar tracking mounting that uses fuzzy logic methods to align the solar panel with the direction of solar irradiation, thereby increasing the solar panel's power output. Data collection is categorized under three weather conditions: sunny, cloudy, and rainy. The results indicate that the error angle ranges from 0.11 ° to 1.58° in sunny weather, 0.01° to 109.93° in cloudy weather, and 0.03° to 47.36° in rainy weather. Using a dual-axis solar tracking system, the power output of PV increased by 35.3 % to 67.3%. Error angle occurs due to the misalignment between the apparent movement of the sun and the direction of the PV module motion. In sunny weather, dual-axis solar tracking can operate optimally, allowing solar panels to align with solar irradiation, thereby increasing generated power output. However, clouds obstruct sunlight in cloudy or rainy conditions, making it difficult for the dual-axis solar tracking to accurately detect the sun's movement.

articleTitle: Comparison Analysis of Forecasting Accuracy for Electricity Consumption Using Extreme Learning Machine and Backpropagation Algorithms
abstract: Accurate calculations are essential in forecasting. Therefore, it is important to select the appropriate forecasting method, which can be determined by testing the accuracy level of the forecasting results using the MAPE value. The purpose of this research is to analyze the comparison of the accuracy of electricity consumption forecasts using the Extreme Learning Machine and Backpropagation algorithms. The data used are monthly electricity consumption data as input pattern designs. The input data will be divided into two parts: training data and testing data, followed by simulations using the Extreme Learning Machine and Backpropagation algorithms to obtain the 2022 forecast results. The accuracy of each algorithm's forecast results will then be calculated using the MAPE value. The research results indicate that the Extreme Learning Machine algorithm has a MAPE value of 4.67%, where the error rate is higher than the Backpropagation algorithm, which has only 2.27%. From the algorithm testing stages, the most accurate forecasting result for electricity consumption was obtained using Backpropagation, as it has the lowest MAPE value, indicating the highest accuracy and lowest error rate.

articleTitle: Speed Motor and Temperature Controller for Coffee Roasting Machine Using PID
abstract: Control techniques are used during the coffee roasting process to enhance the quality of roasted beans. The roasting machine features a drum and motor that rotates to prevent burning. The aim of this research is to design an efficient control system for a coffee roasting machine using PID methods to ensure consistent temperature and drum speed throughout the roasting process. By implementing both open-loop and closed-loop Ziegler-Nichols tuning, this study seeks to optimize machine performance for different roast levels, minimizing steady-state error (Ess) and improving the overall quality of roasted coffee beans. The process starts by heating the drum to 150 degrees Celsius, then adjusting the temperature to achieve the desired roast level. The PID control method is used to maintain consistent temperature and drum rotation speed. The Ziegler-Nichols open-loop tuning method provides the control parameters for temperature regulation, with Kp (33.99) and Ki (0.39). Meanwhile, the closed-loop Ziegler-Nichols method is applied for controlling drum speed, resulting in Kp (3.6), Ki (2.4), and Kd (1.35). Testing at different roast levels (light, medium, and dark) showed Ess values of 0.24 percent, 2.2 percent, and 0.067 percent, respectively. Additionally, during motor speed testing, the lowest Ess was 0.5 percent at 300 rpm. These findings validate the success of the PID and PI control methods in optimizing the coffee roasting machine's performance, contributing to better quality roasted beans.

articleTitle: Frequency Control of Interconnected Power System Utilizing Novel Optimization Approaches
abstract: Electrical power systems nowadays are complex and interfered with each other in areas and divisions. In order to link multiple areas of power systems, an Automatic Generation Control (AGC) is required to control voltage and frequency. The control on frequency is affected by load change in the areas of power systems. Load Frequency Control (LFC) is mandatory to maintain system stability and efficiency. In this paper, three classical controllers are applied to a two area LFC system with a target of error minimization by Integral Square Error (ISE) function. The three controllers are Fractional Filtered PID Controller (PIDNF), Fractional Filtered FOPID Controller (FOPIDNF), and Sigmoid PID Controller (SPID). These controllers are tuned by novel optimization algorithms which are Giant Trevally Optimizer (GTO), Tasmanian Devil Optimizer (TDO), and Zebra Optimization Algorithm (ZOA). The best optimization results were obtained from the GTO-SPID controller combination.

articleTitle: BLDC Motor Sizing Analysis on P1 Topology Hybridization of Single Cylinder ICE
abstract: The hybridization process of a motorcycle with a P1 configuration identifies the performance of an electric motor at the same speed point or more on an internal combustion engine (ICE). The targeted speed is the highest torque point on the ICE. This condition is often called torque assist. Most starter motors on conventional motorcycles operate at cranking speed. The use of starter motors in the latest technology uses a BLDC electric motor. The advancement of controllers and starter motor topology enables the BLDC electric motor to run at its maximum torque point speed on the ICE. Generally., ICE designs that have BLDC electric motors use P1 hybrid topology or are often called integrated starter-generator (ISG). The paper focuses on the analysis of the sizing of BLDC electric motors to be able to operate as ISGs at the highest torque point speed on the ICE. The constraints in the paper are in the form of operating voltage parameters., wire diameter., and number of turns. Changes in these values achieve a greater motor torque equal to its base torque and a motor speed greater than its base speed. The sizing results show an increase in speed of up to 3000 rpm with operating temperature conditions for 60 minutes maintained at 50.2 °C. The reduction in fuel consumption during vehicle dynamics testing reached 1,376% in the ECE-R15 driving cycle, 1,033 in the ECE-R40 driving cycle, and 1,217 in the WMTC driving cycle.

articleTitle: Modeling and Output Feedback Control Design of a CoreXY System
abstract: This paper presents the modeling and feedback control design methods of a CoreXY system platform. The proposed design method includes derivation of both kinematics and dynamics models of the platform using geometric and Euler- Lagrange equation analyses. The linear quadratic Gaus-sian (LQG) control method is then constructed based on the estimation of the system's state variables that are obtained using Kalman filter algorithm. Bryson's rule is used to tune the LQG control parameters to achieve the desired performance of the closed loop output feedback control systems. Simulation results are presented to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed output feedback control system to control the CoreXY's end frame from an initial position coordinate to a desired final position.

articleTitle: The Influence of Parallel Multigap Rod Electrodes on the Breakdown Probability Distribution
abstract: Increasing the capacity and operating voltage of an electrical equipment commonly also requires increasing its dimensions. The geometrical change of the electrical equipment parts will influence the distribution of the electric field and the probability distribution of the breakdown voltage. Based on Ohm's Law, increasing the dimensions between two line-conductors can reduce the insulation strength between the two conductors. In this paper, an observation is focused on the dimensional change of parallel rod-electrodes arrangement in the air dielectric. The dimensional change is realized through the variations of the rod-electrodes number. Variations of one pair up to five pairs of rod electrodes are studied with the air gap between the electrodes of 1.5 cm, the diameter of 1.5 cm and the distance between the parallel electrode-pairs of 1.25 cm. The result of the research show that increasing the number of pairs of rod electrodes in parallel shifts the graph of the distribution function or cumulative probability of breakdown voltage, indicating the importance of considering the geometrical enlargement aspect in designing electrical equipment.

articleTitle: Performance of DCT-DWT Feature Extraction in Recognizing Guitar Chords
abstract: This work deals with optimization problems in the field of audio signals with particular emphasis on recognizing guitar chords. As an extension to the previous works done in this field, the primary goal was to minimize the feature extraction length without loss of recognition performance. In this case, this work used two such well known methods in audio signal processing as the Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) and the Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT). This method is based on the iterative analysis of three main system attributes: the frame blocking length; the choice of wavelet functions; and the DWT coefficient selection offset. After careful tuning of these parameters, this work was able to optimize the feature extraction length to only three, which however represents a modest improvement on the previous works in this field. The system developed in this research obtained recognition accuracy of up to 91.43% when the optimized feature extraction length was employed. The significance of this study extends to the non-conventional applications of guitar chord recognition. Shortening the feature extraction length is expected to improve more usages in the different applications of the music technology.

articleTitle: Simulation of a Single-Phase Bidirectional DC-AC Converter Using Hysteresis Current Control Method with DC Bus Voltage Regulation Based on Fuzzy Logic
abstract: The energy transition to new renewable energy (RNE) is becoming inevitable with rapid technological development. One is the development of electric vehicle technology with the Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) concept that allows vehicles to transfer power back to the grid when needed. For this, a DC-AC bidirectional converter is required that is capable of flowing power in two directions, in both rectifier and inverter operating modes. The topology used is a Single Phase Full-Bridge Current-Controlled Voltage Source Inverter (CC- VSI) with hysterical current control method and Fuzzy Logic-based voltage regulation. The study aims to analyze the characteristics of the operating mode as well as the response of the system. To obtain the result to keep the voltage of the DC bus at the nominal value, a combination of load/ current injection against the corresponding reference current is required. The hysterical signal frequency range is obtained to match the design and simulation in the frequencies of 7.5-15 kHz. The rectifier mode is characterized by the phase difference between the AC current and its voltage. Instead, the inverter mode has the same phase between the two. The fuzzy logic voltage regulation allows the stability of the DC bus awake in the presence of dynamic change of load/ inj ection of current with a sufficiently fast system response at settling times ranging from 1–4 seconds.

articleTitle: Vulnerability Analysis on Internet of Things (IoT) Networks using Raspberry Pi and Open Web Application Security Project (OWASP)
abstract: The security of a network supports a system so that every device is in a safe condition, with secure communication, and secure access control to every asset in the IoT ecosystem. Some previous research references make the topic of discussion in this research, namely security on IoT servers. On that basis, the idea was created to conduct vulnerability analysis on the IoT network using Raspberry Pi and OWASP (Open Web Application Security Project). The application of OWASP in IoT networks has proven successful on Raspberry Pi because of its flexibility compared to Personal Computer (PC). This is evidenced when an attack on a local network server is carried out, 7 types of vulnerabilities are found and then the stages of solving solutions to vulnerabilities on the server are carried out. The highest level of vulnerability obtained is categorized as “Medium” and the lowest level obtained is categorized as “Low”. So, the conclusion of this research states that the highest vulnerability is obtained in the cloud hosting network type because it is connected to the internet, and it becomes a different thing on a local network that is only connected to a local area network.

articleTitle: Real-time Potholes Detection and Localization using YOLOv8
abstract: The maintenance of road infrastructure involves significant efforts, and the detection of potholes is key to identifying areas in need of repair. In this research, we propose an innovative approach by combining YOLOv8, the eighth version of the You Only Look Once (YOLO) architecture, and the Roboflow platform to enhance accuracy and efficiency in pothole detection. Our approach begins with the collection of a dataset encompassing various road conditions and pothole sizes. We preprocess the data using Roboflow to ensure dataset consistency and quality. YOLO- 8 is then trained using the processed dataset, harnessing the power of deep learning technology to produce a superior object detection model. With YOLOv8, we present a reliable solution for real-time monitoring and maintenance of pothole-ridden roads. The implementation of this technology is expected to support more effective road infrastructure management, enabling swift responses to road conditions requiring repair. This research contributes to the development of an efficient and innovative pothole detection system.

articleTitle: Harmonic Distortion Reduction Analysis of Railway Static Inverter Output Using Passive Filter and PI Controller with Matlab Simulink
abstract: Static Inverter (SIV) is one type of inverter used in Indonesian trains. The use of inverters in the Static Inverter (SIV) still uses a Two Level Inverter (2LI). The application of Two Level Inverter (2LI) still has shortcomings in the Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) value which is still high. This research presents a control strategy for a Static Inverter (SIV) in a load-connected three-phase system. The system consists of a DC source, inverter, 2nd order RLC passive filter, transformer, and auxiliary loads. The main objectives of the strategy are to reduce the voltage and current overshoot after the installation of the RLC passive filter, reduce harmonics, reference the 380 V voltage value, stabilize the voltage and current and create an optimal output waveform. The control strategy is done by optimizing the Proportional Integral (PI) controller through voltage controlled Sinusoidal Pulse With Modulation (SPWM) method. The system model and control strategy are implemented using MATLAB/SIMULINK software (Version R2021a). The results show that the implemented control strategy can provide low THD values in the 110 kVA Static Inverter (SIV), namely 0.90%,0.47 %, 0.66 % for THDv in the RST phase and 0.53%, 0.79%, 0.43% for THDi in the RST phase with a steady state at 0.04s with an output voltage of 380 V and minimize the overshoot in the output waveform.

articleTitle: LTE-Advanced Network Planning with Inter-Band Non-Contiguous Carrier Aggregation in Mampang Prapatan
abstract: Mampang Prapatan is a very strategic area of health facilities, education centers, shopping centers, sports facilities, etc. Mampang Prapatan has an average resource block usage of 83. 755% or close to the operator's standard limit. KPI (Key Performance Indicator) operators, issue a standard for the use of RB (Resource Blocks), which is a maximum of 90%. If the percentage of RB is almost or even reaches 90%, then the site is declared to be experiencing user overload which has an impact on low throughput acceptance. This research using CA (Carrier Aggregation) method by combining 1800MHz and 2100MHz, each of which has a bandwidth of 10MHz. The simulation is carried out with two scenarios. The first scenario uses an 1800 MHz cell as the PCC (Primary Component Carrier). Whereas in the second scenario, the 2100MHz cell is the PCC. This research influences LTE-A network performance by implementing carrier aggregation. The average SINR (Signal to Interference Noise ratio) result was 11.67 dB with an increase of 89.45%. The average RSRP (Reference Signal Received Power) result was 83.41 dBm with an increase of 7.80% and an average throughput result obtained of 17622. 75Kbps with an increase of 67.83%.

articleTitle: Modeling and Cascade PID Controller Design of a Spinbath Circulation Process
abstract: This paper reports the development of a cascade PID type control scheme for a MIMO spinbath circulation process regulation. In the proposed scheme, the dynamic model of the complete spinbath circulation process is first developed using concepts from fluid dynamics. Reduction of the obtained model through lumping of identical processes as well as linearization techniques is then conducted to obtain a simplified MIMO linear system with cascading control structure. A cascade PI control configuration is then constructed to achieve simultaneous control objectives in the interacting process variables of the developed simplified model [1]–[3]. More specifically, the proposed cascade controller is of the type of summed setpoint cascade PI that is selected for its cost-effectiveness and computational efficiency. It combines a summed setpoints to simultaneously manages multiple inputs, as well as cascades of faster inner disturbance rejection to allow for the minimization of the overall process' output deviations. Simulation results for constant as well as changing setpoints are then presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed modeling and cascade control schemes.

articleTitle: Smart Control Design Battery Charger with Sampling Method for Lithium-Ion
abstract: In accordance with its various advantages, Lithiumion batteries are widely used as secondary batteries (rechargeable batteries). The smart charging method will be applied according to the characteristics of the factory. The charging voltage and current are determined by the Sampling Method, where the voltage is monitored periodically during the charging process according to the specific needs of the battery used. This technique ensures that the voltage remains at a safe position, optimizes the charging speed, and prevents excess current that can damage the charged battery. Experimental activities were carried out to validate the proposed method, testing battery charging at three capacity levels: therefore the percentage of 0% as the case of battery capacity in the uncharged position, 50% as the case of half-charged battery capacity and in transition to full, and 80% as the case of full battery capacity will be used in this study. Experiments have shown deviation values of 0.040818, 0.00333, and 0.0087 for each competency level as explained below. These deviations correlate PPC in terms of capacity value, meaning that the ratio is proportional. These findings indicate that the Sampling Method provides a good solution to address the resistance changes as useful evidence for smart charging strateaies.

articleTitle: Variable Speed Drive of Three Phase Induction Motor Based on Internet of Things
abstract: Variable Speed Drive of Three Phase Squirrel Cage Induction Motor (SCIM) based on Internet of Things is a study that aims to control the speed and direction of rotation of a three phase induction motor using a variable speed drive based on IoT (Internet of Things). This control system is implemented on a 0.75kw induction motor connected to a mechanical load, namely a DC generator, the speed of which is controlled using a Variable Speed Drive Sinamic G120 which is controlled using a PLC (Programmable Logic Controller) Siemens S7 1200. This control system can be monitored with a multi-display via the Human Machine Interface (HMI) Simatic KTP 700 Comfort which is connected with an ethernet cable, then a PC (Personal Computer) Server, PC (Personal Computer) Client and Smartphone connected via the internet. Programming is done using the TIA Portal and Wincc Unifield applications. The test results show that this control system can be monitored and has worked well, the PC server display, the PC client and Smartphone have successfully displayed the monitored motor data and have also successfully controlled the motor as desired.

articleTitle: Dynamic Emission Dispatch using Quadratic Constrained Programming
abstract: This paper explores the implementation of Dynamic Emission Dispatch (DED) using Quadratic Constrained Programming (QCP) to minimize emissions from thermal generators while ensuring a reliable power supply in the electrical grid, even under challenging conditions. Traditional dispatch methods often overlook environmental impacts, but DED integrates real-time data, advanced predictive techniques, and adaptive algorithms to dynamically meet stringent emission limits. By utilizing QCP, DED accurately models the complex, non-linear characteristics of power generation and emissions, optimizing the dispatch schedule under varying operational conditions. This adaptability is essential for managing the complexities of power systems, including fluctuating demand, diverse generation sources, and evolving regulatory requirements. This study focuses on the IEEE 30 bus system, comparing QCP with the Lambda Iteration method to demonstrate the practical applicability and effectiveness of the proposed approach. The results indicate that DED with QCP significantly reduces emissions compared to traditional methods like Lambda Iteration, while maintaining grid reliability and supporting environmental sustainability.

articleTitle: Comparison of W-Lambert and F-Solve Methods in Micro Solar Cell Modeling
abstract: Recent advancements in photovoltaic technology and micro solar cells aim to extend smartphone battery life through renewable energy sources. However, integrating micro solar cells presents challenges, particularly with low output voltage. This study uses Matlab simulations to address this issue and compare the W-Lambert function's effectiveness with the f-solve method. The results indicate that the f-solve method, especially with the trust-region algorithm, outperforms the W-Lambert function in modeling the 1- V characteristics of micro-PV cells for smartphone charging applications. The f-solve method provides more accurate predictions with lower error rates and is more effective in determining series and shunt resistances. The method achieved an output voltage of 200 m V and a power output of 1.49 μ W, representing a 0.67% improvement over previous studies. These findings suggest that f-solve can enhance the efficiency and performance of micro-PV cell-based charging systems. Further research is recommended to optimize this model under various and complex environmental conditions. This study offers valuable insights into the selection of modeling techniques and supports the advancement of sustainable energy solutions for mobile devices.

articleTitle: Application of Carbon Nanoparticles with Arc-Discharge Synthesis as an Anode Material in Lithium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are a type of rechargeable secondary battery consisting of electrodes (anode and cathode), a separator, and an electrolyte. The commonly used anode material is graphite powder. Recently, carbon nanotubes (CNTs) have also begun to be researched for their application as electrodes in batteries. The advantage of nanoparticle technology is its openness to being combined with other technologies, thereby opening opportunities to create better delivery systems. In this research, lithium-ion batteries were fabricated with the addition of nanoparticles as the anode. The purpose of this study is to compare lithium-ion batteries with anodes made of graphite material, CNTs synthesized by arc-discharge with a current variation of 40A, and combinations of graphite with CNTs 40A, graphite with MWCNTs, and CNTs 40A with MWCNTs in terms of maximum capacity and time during the charge and discharge process. The results of this study show that batteries with anodes made of a mixture of graphite and CNTs 40A have better maximum capacity compared to batteries with other anode materials, reaching 0.40 Ah during charging and 0.23 Ah during discharging in the first cycle. Batteries with anodes made of a mixture of CNTs 40A and MWCNTs have the fastest charging and discharging process, reaching 28436 seconds during charging and 7563 seconds during discharging in the 5th cycle.

articleTitle: Implementation of ADAS for Electric Vehicle Safety for Pediatric Patients Based on Fuzzy Logic
abstract: The implementation of an Advanced Driver Assistance System (ADAS) for electric vehicles used in transporting pediatric patients in a hospital setting can significantly enhance safety and comfort. This study aims to develop and implement a Fuzzy Logic-based Advanced Driver Assistance System (ADAS) to enhance the safety of electric transportation for pediatric patients in hospitals. The system utilizes Light Detection and Ranging (LIDAR) sensors and rotary encoders to detect distance and speed, while employing fuzzy control to regulate braking and avoid collisions. Testing of the ADAS with fuzzy logic yielded promising results in improving the safety of electric vehicles for pediatric patients. This is evident from the system's ability to swiftly respond to dynamic obstacles and effectively manage braking across various LIDAR detection ranges. The fuzzy system facilitates more flexible handling of uncertainties in dynamic environments, which is particularly crucial in a hospital setting with considerable activity and movement. The test results indicate that the sensors and fuzzy algorithms used in the system had a low error rate, with the highest being 5.90%. The system performed well in various dynamic and static conditions, stopping within the targeted distance in all scenarios. However, under loaded conditions, the speed during moderate braking fluctuated slightly (16 cm/s to 14 cm/s) at moderate PWM. Usability testing suggests that the system is generally well-received by users, although there remains room for further improvement.

articleTitle: River Detection Using Fast Fourier Transform, Contour Detection, and Hough Line Transform
abstract: River environment presents significant challenges compared to the marine environment due to its diverse and complex features. Processing data from rivers, particularly image data, is inherently difficult because of this complexity. This paper presents a method for detecting river areas in images using a Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), contour detection, and Hough line transform. The method leverages the characteristic of water surfaces having a uniform color, which results in distinct low-frequency components in the frequency domain. By this characteristic, the proposed system effectively identifies river regions with high accuracy. The methodology encompasses several crucial steps: image pre-processing, application of the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) to analyze frequency components, thresholding to isolate significant frequencies, noise reduction through contour selection, and line detection using the Hough Line Transform. The proposed method has been tested on a diverse dataset of river images, demonstrating an impressive accuracy of up to 98%. This approach offers a robust solution for river detection, effectively addressing the challenges posed by varying river environments.

articleTitle: Implementation and Design of Fiber to the Building using Higher Splitter Ratio Method
abstract: The development of telecommunication data exchanges very fast nowadays due to the trend of user demand. Optical fiber transmission has been widely used in addressing every telecommunication service need, this research offers the concept of FTTB. This research method uses a higher split ratio to improve the QoS of FTTB based on GPON (Gigabit Passive Optical Network). Subsequently, the results are assessed and scrutinized, focusing on the link power budget parameters to ensure compatibility with optical network feasibility. The FTTB is concentrated at the JC (Joint Closure) location with users including Tunas Ridean Building (Loc-1), Tafakul Insurance Building (Loc-2), and Panin Bank Building (Loc-3). The location from the CO (Central Office) to the ODP (Optical Distribution Point) is 1.88km. Then, ODP to JC is 0.15km. Next, JC to OTB Loc-1 is 0.22km. Subsequently, the distance from JC to OTB Loc-2 is 0.06 km, while it is 0.11 km to OTB Loc-3. The comprehensive assessment reveals that the power link budget acquired remains below the receiver sensitivity threshold of -28dBm. Ultimately, the findings affirm the effective deployment of the FTTB network utilizing the higher split ratio approach, particularly suitable for densely populated office structures.

articleTitle: Hydrothermal Growth of Semiconducting Zinc Oxide for Ethanol Sensor Application
abstract: Ethanol is a volatile organic compound widely used in various industries. It is commonly found as a colorless, liquid substance. Ethanol has a low flash point of 14–16 °C which brings around a fire hazard. It also poses health risks such as skin, eyes, and respiratory irritation, nausea, vomiting, and intoxication. Ethanol gas sensors have been utilized to mitigate these risks and hazards. The development of ethanol gas sensors has been concentrated on improving sensitivity and selectivity. Zinc Oxide (ZnO) has been one of the most promising active materials for ethanol sensors due to their strong surface interaction. This work aims to fabricate an ethanol sensor based on hydrothermally grown ZnO. Hydrothermal growths were performed using zinc acetate dihydrate (ZAD) and hexamethylenetetramine (HMTA) for 6 hours at 90°C. Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</inf>0<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> (001) was employed as the substrate. The silver paste was applied and annealed on the grown ZnO to fabricate a conductivity-based ethanol sensor. The Figaro SR-3 system was utilized to conduct gas sensing tests. The effects of the precursor concentration ratio and its total concentration on the morphology of the grown ZnO were investigated. A shift in growth mode was observed by SEM. FTIR and XRD were used to confirm the formation of hexagonal ZnO on sapphire. The sample grown at a total concentration of 0.3 M, ZAD: HMTA concentration ratios of 3: 1 showed a coalesced island morphology. The gas sensing test indicated a positive correlation between conductivity and ethanol concentration.

articleTitle: Design of IoT-Based Ground Resistance Monitoring and Control Systems
abstract: The grounding system has an important role in securing electrical equipment, humans, the environment, and the surroundings from excessive voltage spikes by flowing electric current to the ground as the neutral point. Based on PUIL 2011, the maximum ground resistance is 5 ohms therefore electric current can flow. However, natural conditions sometimes allow the ground resistance to exceed 5 ohms. The impact of weather changes such as rainfall also affects the effectiveness of the grounding system. Therefore, this paper proposes the Design of an Internet of Things-Based Ground Resistance Monitoring and Control System, which is useful for maximizing preventive measures against the threat of lightning strikes and other disturbances as well as monitoring and controlling the value of ground resistance automatically to facilitate the performance of humans or operators in the field. The resulting system error is 3.03 %, and the system precision is 0.16 %. From the test results, it is known that the tool functions properly to reduce the value of ground resistance, and this value can be monitored by IoT.

articleTitle: Analysis of Weather Changes on the Performance of On-Grid Solar Power Plants at the Qosim Al-Hadi Islamic Boarding School, Mijen, Semarang
abstract: PV Generators are currently in high demand as a substitute for electricity usage from the State Electricity Company (PLN). However, PV Generator performance is uncertain due to weather influences. This paper discusses the relationship between weather changes and PV performance at the Qosim AI-Hadi Islamic Boarding School in Mijen, Semarang City. Weather data were obtained from secondary sources provided by the Meteorology and Geophysics Agency, with October representing the rainy season and January representing the dry season. Four weather variables were considered: air temperature, humidity, rainfall, and the duration of sun shines. This weather data were then correlated with primary data from the installed PV Generator system, including current in amperes (A) and electrical power in kW. The results of the statistical analysis show that the average electric current generated in the dry season is 4.46 A, while in the rainy season, it averages 2.81 A. Meanwhile, the power generated during the dry and rainy seasons averages 1.11 kW and 0.53 kW, respectively. These results indicate that the efficiency of the PV Generator decreases by 47.7% during the rainy season. This reduction is due to the minimal sunlight exposure during the rainy season, as it is often obstructed by clouds.

articleTitle: Control and Monitoring System for Aeroponic Lettuce Spraying using Logistic Regression
abstract: Urban agriculture has become increasingly popular as communities seek to maximize available space for food cultivation. Aeroponics, a technique where plants are suspended and nutrient solutions are sprayed directly onto their roots, is one of these innovative farming methods. Although aeroponics offers efficiency benefits over traditional systems, it also presents challenges in complexity. Leveraging modern technology, this study introduces a control and monitoring system tailored for aeroponic lettuce cultivation. Utilizing an ESP32 microcontroller integrated with DHT22, water level, and TDS sensors, the system adjusts nutrient delivery based on temperature and humidity conditions, with real-time monitoring available via a web interface. By automating the pumping mechanism to align with environmental parameters, this system optimizes lettuce growth and conserves water more efficiently than standard methods.

articleTitle: Assessing Food Photo Aesthetics Through Dominant Color and Color Harmony with Adaptive Smoothing Regularization
abstract: This study explores the enhancement of aesthetic evaluation for food photographs by integrating Adaptive Smoothing Regularization (ASR) with key visual features, including Dominant Color (DC) and Color Harmony (CH). Addressing the critical challenge of accurately assessing the aesthetic quality of food images a factor essential to digital marketing and consumer engagement the research employs a variety of machine learning models such as Support Vector Machine (SVM), Decision Tree (DT), Random Forest (RF), Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), and deep learning models like InceptionV3,trained both with and without ASR on a publicly available food image dataset. The results demonstrate a significant improvement in model performance when ASR is combined with DC and CH features. Notably, the InceptionV3+ASR model using only DC achieved the highest sensitivity in identifying aesthetically pleasing images, outperforming other models regarding recall and Fl-score. The MLP+ASR model, when utilizing both DC and CH features, showed further enhancements, though with a slight decrease in sensitivity due to the added complexity of CH. Overall, integrating ASR with carefully selected visual features proves to be a robust approach for improving the accuracy and reliability of automated aesthetic assessments.

articleTitle: Navigation System in Dynamic Indoor Environment using Deep Reinforcement Learning with Actor-Critic
abstract: The challenge of mobile robot navigation system is how to find the optimal path and be able to avoid obstacles. The obstacles could be stationary or moving objects, which make the environment of mobile robot would be changed dynamically. Regarding this problem, the conventional method should update the path everytime when there are any changes in environment, so it causes the computational burden. This paper aims to solve the problem by developing Deep Reinforcement Learning with Actor-Critic (DRL-AC) as navigation method to find the optimal path. DRL-AC determines robot movement by selecting action which have highest reward. DRL-AC is developed with actor and critic neural networks which are trained in dynamic environment. To prevent hardware damages during the training process, DRL-AC is developed in simulator. This simulator is designed to adopt real world condition. After training, DRL-AC can be implemented to the real mobile robot. The performance of DRL-AC is analyzed through neuron dimension and how the mobile robot navigated successfully in dynamic environment. The training results show that neural network with 2048 x 1024 hidden layer started to be convergent and mobile robot navigated successfully to avoid obstacle.

articleTitle: Design of Control and Monitoring System in the Development of CNC Machines for Plasma-Based Scanning Probe
abstract: The development of nanotechnology encourages the need for an efficient control and monitoring system on CNC (Computer Numerical Control) machines developed specifically for plasma-based Scanning Probe applications. This research focuses on designing motor control systems on CNC machines and monitoring current and voltage in plasma generation modules. The Universal G-Code Sender firmware is used as the stepper motor movement control, while the plasma generation module uses a 20kV High Voltage Pressure Generator Igniter Step Up Boost integrated on the CNC machine to support plasma-based probe scanning. The monitoring system is made using ZMCT103C sensors to read the current and differential circuit amplifiers to read the voltage in real-time. Testing the control system on the stepper motor using the jog controller on the Universal G-Code Sender is able to run according to the given command, which is as far as 1 mm per step for the X and Y axes. The highest voltage before plasma discharge is 3,069.9 V, the lowest voltage is 2,013.6 V. The highest voltage when plasma discharge occurs is 1,427.5 V, and the lowest voltage is 430,108 V. While the largest current when plasma discharge occurs is 0.13 A, the lowest current is 0.09 A. When there is no plasma discharge, the reading current is zero.

articleTitle: Parameter Estimation of Two-Element Rectangular Microstrip Patch Antenna Using Artificial Neural Network
abstract: The process of estimating the parameters of rectangular patch microstrip antennas has so far had some shortcomings, such as the amount of error generated and the complexity of the method. Therefore, research is needed to develop a new method that can improve the results of estimating the parameters, reducing the error rate and simplifying the process. An estimator model based on Artificial Neural Network (ANN) is proposed to analyse and estimate the parameters of a two-element rectangular patch microstrip antenna, including directivity, resonant frequency, VSWR, gain, bandwidth, and return loss. The data values input into the ANN include the substrate's dielectric constant, the substrate's thickness, and the feed and patch's length and width. The results show that the ANN can estimate the parameters of a two-element rectangular patch microstrip antenna with a low error rate and good convergence with low Mean Squared Error (MSE) value for directivity, resonant frequency, VSWR, gain, bandwidth, and return loss parameters of 0.00862, 0.02440, 0.00228, 0.04352, 0.00004, and 0.10232, respectively. The evaluation results demonstrate that our proposed ANN model have increased the accuracy estimation rate of two-element rectangular patch microstrip antenna parameters.

articleTitle: Torque and Flux Characteristic of IPMSMs with Various Rotor Constructions
abstract: The efficiency of an electric motor will always be the primarily concern in the machine design. It will moreover be the target during the improvement of the electric motor construction. One of the electric motors that is currently undergoing rapid development is interior permanent magnets synchronous motors, IPMSMs. In IPMSMs, permanent magnets are embedded in the rotor core. With this construction, IPMSMs have a rigid body, therefore it can be applied at medium to very high speeds. Other advantages of the machine is that it allows to achieve high efficiency, and high power density. Common designs found in IPMSMs are V-Shape, U-Shape, and Flat-shape. These designs are categorized based on the shape of the magnet slots used in the rotor. The efficiency of the three designs is quite capable compared to its predecessor model, namely SPMSMs. This efficiency is related with the flux distribution profile. In this paper, the torque profile and air gap flux distribution of the motors are compared using FEA simulations.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Multiple Machine Learning Models Applied to Dissolved Gas Analysis Under Thermal Fault Classification Considering IEEE C57.104-2019TM Standard for Substation Transformer
abstract: The use of Dissolved Gas Analysis (DGA) as a non-intrusive test for assessing transformer health is widespread in the field. However, traditional DGA-based diagnostics have several limitations. The Rogers ratio method is confined to gases involved in the computation, the interpretation of the IEC Ratio method can be ambiguous, and the Duval triangle method is unable to differentiate between healthy and faulty oil degradation. Furthermore, these traditional methods rely on subjective judgment from experts. To address these shortcomings, a two-layer framework has been proposed in this paper. The framework utilizes the random forest algorithm with the IEEE C57.104 - 2019TM guide as a watchdog in the first layer to distinguish between unhealthy and normal oil degradation. The second layer employs a neural network to classify different thermal fault occurences in the transformer. Traditional methods like Doernenburg, Duval, Rogers, and IEC ratio methods have been used for years, with Duval Triangle showing the best accuracy at 87.18%. Machine learning methods outperform traditional ones, with Support Vector Machine achieving 95.70% and Neural Networks reaching the highest accuracy of 97.90%. Despite high accuracy, the machine learning framework faced challenges due to a limited and imbalanced dataset.

articleTitle: Optimizing Data Transfer through Duplication for Increased Energy Efficiency in Green Internet of Things
abstract: The rapid growth of the Internet of Things (loT) is increasing its application across various fields, leading to higher annual electrical power consumption. To enhance energy conservation in loT usage, it is essential to reduce the data files of Wireless Sensor Networks (WSN) sensors. Large data volumes prolong the processing and transmission times, thereby consuming more electricity. Transmission can be minimized if sensor node data are repetitive by avoiding the repeated sending of unchanged data. The data-duplication detection method identifies previously sent data, eliminating the need for retransmission unless there are changes in order or magnitude. The test results indicate that the duplication detection process effectively identifies the sent data. The relationship between file size and power consumption is evident: 56-byte files consume 1.808 watts, 29-byte files consume 1.795 watts, and 8-byte files consume 1.793 watts.

articleTitle: The Design and Implementation of an IoT-Supported Collaborative Learning Media
abstract: The application layer of the IoT architecture can guarantee a large number of users will receive same data and information in real time. These features and services will be used as a fundamental idea to create and develop the IoT -supported collaborative learning media. Next a conceptual design of the IoT -supported collaborative learning media is created and proposed. The overall research through four main stages: literature studies, observation and analysis on the practicum class of renewable energy, formulating the conceptual design of an IoT -supported learning media to support collaborative learning and developing an IoT -supported collaborative learning media as a proof of concept. Google spreadsheet is utilized to realize in the middleware layer that supporting the services in application layer. As the research result, a conceptual design of IoT -based learning media to support collaborative learning has been developed and issued. Furthermore, a trainer kit to support collaborative learning in renewable energy class has been developed as a proof of concept. The test results show that the IoT -supported learning media (trainer kit) can be used in the PLTS renewable energy practicum with several students and the lecturer to perform collaborative learning together. Since there are no handwriting activity, the students and lecturer together can monitor, study and analyzing the main parameters of PLTS in real time manner. This also proves that the conceptual design can be used as a reference while developing a trainer kit for supporting collaborative learning in renewable energy class.

articleTitle: Wireless Sensor Network for Power Control and Monitoring Public Street Lighting with Earthquake Early Warning
abstract: Nowadays, there is a phenomenon known as the annual growth in electrical energy consumption, particularly in the case of Public Street Lighting (PSL) bulbs. Almost all the roads are visible as public ones, and the highway is equipped with PSL lighting. PSL lamps are positioned at a 30-meter interval between each of the left and right median lights. The PIK2 project is the subject of the research for this international collaboration. The road length at the PSL lamp installation position is ±1.8 km. The PSL lamps are 250 watts in power. The specific goal of this research is to use microcontrollers, sensors, and LoRa to design and analyze power, voltage, and current measurements in PSL lamps as well as to control and monitor the condition of PSL lamps through the Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) and apply a star topology for the efficiency of electrical energy consumption in PSL lamps. It is anticipated that this study would result in a best practice model for the integration of WSN into Indonesia's PSL system, which will then serve as a guide for businesses looking to advance their WSN capabilities and boost their competitiveness internationally. The proposed research methods are quantitative and objective, so this study is applied to acquire and distribute data at PSL light points. The data on the sensor will be sent through the end node which is then sent to the coordinator node or gateway. The sensor data on this tool can be displayed by accessing the ubidots.

articleTitle: Pedestrian Object Distance Prediction on Robot Car Using YOLOv4 and Bounding Box Analysis
abstract: This study focuses on enhancing safety in robot car navigation by developing a pedestrian distance prediction system using the YOLOv4 algorithm and bounding box analysis. YOLOv4, known for its speed and accuracy, efficiently detects pedestrians and estimates their distance from robot cars. The research involves creating datasets with distance variations from 1.5 to 5 meters and utilizing a 40th-order polynomial interpolation model for distance estimation. Results indicate that YOLOv4 offers precise detection, and the interpolation model predicts distances with an average error of 2.69% and a correlation coefficient of 0.9223, improving navigation safety and efficiency in dynamic environments.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Detection of Botnet Attacks in the Internet of Things Networks Through the Utilization of Hybrid Feature Selection
abstract: The proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) technology is leading to an escalation in cyber risks. The Intrusion Detection System (IDS) is crucial in countering cyber threats, with botnets being the most commonly detected attack in IoT networks. Anomaly-based IDS is necessary to enhance their capability in identifying cyber threat attributes through the use of supervised machine learning. This work investigates an enhanced supervised machine learning algorithm technique that combines filter-based feature selection methods, specifically Low Variance and Pearson Correlation Coefficient, to detect a new type of botnet attack. The CICIoT2023 dataset, an updated benchmark intrusion dataset specifically designed for IoT networks, is employed to assess the model's performance using several algorithms including Decision Tree, Random Forest, Logistic Regression, and Naive Bayes. The results demonstrate that the model effectively enhances the identification of botnet attacks by reducing the number of features from 46 to 14. This optimization leads to improved performance, including increased accuracy level and reduced computation time.

articleTitle: Testing and Calibration of Electronic Sensor Devices for Application of Smart Hospital Room Monitoring System
abstract: The quality of the hospital room environment is essential, as infection-causing germs can spread through airborne droplets or direct contact. Several factors, including occupancy density, humidity, lighting, and room temperature, significantly affect the transmission of infections. Therefore, monitoring inpatient rooms in hospitals is a major concern, particularly due to the absence of real-time monitoring for patients with critical conditions. Real-time remote inpatient room monitoring can provide essential information for patients, their families, as well as elderly or chronically ill patients who wish to avoid prolonged hospital stays. Motivated by realizing smart inpatient hospital room monitoring based on Internet of Things (IoT) as our long-term goal, this paper is first stage to discuss the testing and calibration of electronic sensors as part of the long-term goal. In addition, this paper presents also an initial network performance testing. The sensors tested include carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide, humidity (DHT22), temperature (DS18B20), and light (LM393). Calibration is conducted by collecting 50 data points for CO and CO2, each, and 70 data points for each of temperature, humidity, and light. Calibration results indicate that these sensors can be implemented to support a smart hospital room monitoring system. It is clarified by comparing the real testing after calibration. Network testing at various locations shows variations in data transfer and bandwidth, with good data consistency despite environmental factors. Overall, the testing results show good agreement for the usage as a prototype device as part of smart inpatient hospital room monitoring system.

articleTitle: Investigating DDoS Attack Mitigation Strategies and Simulation Tools Using GNS3
abstract: Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks pose a significant threat to network security, necessitating robust defense strategies and effective simulation tools for mitigation. Current DDoS attack modeling and mitigation techniques face challenges in accurately replicating real-world scenarios, hindering the development of effective defense mechanisms. This study aims to address these challenges by investigating the effectiveness of DDoS mitigation approaches and assessing the capabilities of Graphical Network Simulator-3 (GNS3) as a simulation tool for modeling DDoS attacks. This study introduces GNS3 as a practical tool for simulating DDoS attacks and evaluates its effectiveness in comparison with other simulation tools. Additionally, we identified key factors affecting server performance during DDoS attacks, providing insights into defense strategies. Through experimentation and simulation using GNS3, we demonstrated the efficacy of various defense mechanisms in mitigating DDoS attacks. We also highlighted the advantages of GNS3 in providing realistic simulation environments for cybersecurity research. Our findings underscore the importance of accurate DDoS attack modeling and effective defense strategies for enhancing network security resilience. By leveraging advanced simulation tools, such as GNS3, organizations can better prepare for and mitigate the risks posed by DDoS attacks.

articleTitle: Comparative Design of Low Power Half Adder Using MGDIB and CMOS Techniques
abstract: With the growing demand for portable electronic devices and the Internet of Things (IoT), optimizing power efficiency and speed in digital circuit design has become increasingly critical. Arithmetic components, such as half adders, are fundamental to many digital architectures. This research presents a comparative study between a low-power half adder designed using the Modified Gate Diffusion Input (MGDI) technique is a variation of the Gate Diffusion Input (GDI) method, which reduces power consumption and transistor count and an enhanced version with an isolation buffer, termed MGDIB, against a conventional CMOS-based half adder. Circuit designs were implemented using 0.35μm CMOS technology and simulated in LTspice. The performance metrics evaluated include transistor count, leakage current, static power dissipation, and delay. The MGDI half-adder requires only 13 transistors, significantly fewer than the 18 transistors needed by the CMOS design. Furthermore, the MGDIB configuration achieves a substantial reduction in leakage current (0.33 nA compared to 9.81 nA in CMOS) and a shorter delay (0.051 ns compared to 0.52 ns in CMOS). However, the MGDIB half adder exhibits slightly higher static power dissipation (0.11 nW compared to 3.23 nW in CMOS). These findings demonstrate that the MGDI and MGDIB techniques offer substantial improvements in transistor efficiency, operating speed, and power reduction, making them promising approaches for modern digital circuit design.

articleTitle: Field Testing and QoS Analysis of ESP-NOW Communication on ESP32
abstract: This study investigates the performance of the ESP-NOW communication protocol on ESP32 devices through field testing and Quality of Service (QoS) analysis. ESP-NOW is a lightweight, low-energy communication protocol that allows multiple ESP32 devices to communicate without relying on Wi-Fi. The objective of this research is to implement a program capable of measuring QoS parameters, including latency, packet loss, and Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI), across various distances. Field tests were conducted at Tanjungpinang, with devices positioned at heights of 2.5 meters and distances increasing at 10-meter intervals. The results indicate that ESP-NOW communication remains efficient up to 150 meters, with significant performance degradation beyond this range. Latency values ranged from 5.13 ms to 46 ms, and packet loss became substantial beyond 180 meters, with a maximum packet error rate of 99% at 300 meters. RSSI values showed a consistent decrease with increasing distance, falling to -97 dBm at 300 meters. According to TIPHON standards, the latency and packet error rate at closer distances were within acceptable limits, categorizing the protocol's performance as ‘Best’ for latency and ‘Perfect’ to ‘Good’ for packet error rate up to 210 meters. These findings suggest that while ESP-NOW is a viable communication protocol for short to medium distances, its reliability diminishes significantly beyond 200 meters. The study provides valuable insights into the limitations and capabilities of ESP-NOW, aiding users in making informed decisions about its application in various systems. This research supports the use of ESP-NOW in applications requiring robust and efficient short-range communication.

articleTitle: Network Performance Evaluation based on RSSI for Inpatient Room Monitoring Application
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to evaluate the network performance under indoor scenario of wireless sensor network (WSN) between sensor node acting as a client and a server according to distance variation scenario. This work is motivated with a long-term goal to realize remote inpatient room monitoring system applying wearable device. Network performance evaluation in respect to distance variation is carried out. The distance variation is to anticipate that in WSN, nodes can be static or mobile. Network performance evaluation uses three software applications namely inSSIDer, Iperf and Wireshark. Firstly, it is evaluated the distance variations to determine the estimates of network connection based on Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI) for the distance of multiple of 4 meters between an access point and a sensor node starting from 0 m to 20 m. That network connection evaluation applies inSSIDer application. The results are then used to design indoor testing scenario and three schemes of network performance evaluations in term of throughput have been carried out using Iperf and Wireshark applications, namely first scheme applying Wireshark only, second scheme applying iPerf only, and third scheme applying both Wireshark and iPerf simultaneously. The testing for each scheme is then conducted to measure throughput. From the testing results, it can be analyzed distance effect on throughput network performance. The results show the consistency that the farther the location of the sending node, the smaller the signal that can be captured by the receiver, and vice versa. Furthermore, there is a throughput difference when testing is carried out using Wireshark and iPerf applications although it is not significant and both applications are feasible for local network performance test. Our network layout scenario is feasible for the indoor network scenario in supporting our long-term goal of inpatient room monitoring system.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Soft FFR Scheme in RIS-Aided Ultra Dense Femto-Macrocellular Network
abstract: Ultra Dense Network (UDN) and Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS) are known as latest technologies that can enhance system capacity and performance. Deployment of RIS in UDN can overcome the signal blockages that is common in urban areas where UDN applied. However, due to dense deployed small cells, i.e. femtocell in macrocellular network, co-channel interference in UDN faces challenging problem. Applying RIS in UDN can encounter the interference problems more challenging. This paper applies soft FFR scheme in RIS-aided UDN cellular network to investigate its effects in mitigating interference problems in RIS-aided UDN cellular network. Simulation experiment has been carried to evaluate the performance of such RIS-aided UDN network. Three parameters are used to evaluate the performance of network under study, namely Signal-to- Interference plus Noise Ratio (SINR), throughput and Bit Error Rate (BER). The outcomes of the simulation for the network with soft FFR are compared to the network without FFR scheme, referred to as baseline system. The simulation results show that the SINR of femtocell for the network with soft FFR scheme increases 3.07 dB, throughput increases 9.99 Mbps and BER decreases from 2.96 x 10–<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> to 5.73 X 10-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup>• The system with soft FFR scheme outperforms the baseline system and soft FFR is promising to reduce the interference effects in RIS-aided UDN network.

articleTitle: Multilevel Selection Keyboard with Huffman Encoding for Individuals with Upper Limb Disabilities
abstract: This study evaluated the performance of three keyboard layouts: T9, hierarchical character selection, and Huffman encoding-based systems. Five participants were tasked with typing six sentences, including three pangrams and three simple sentences, all in the national language to minimize language-related difficulties. The total time taken to type each sentence was recorded for analysis. The results indicate a clear hierarchy in performance, with the T9 keyboard consistently outperforming the other two layouts. The T9 keyboard proved to be the most efficient, showing significantly shorter typing times compared to the hierarchical character selection and Huffman encoding-based keyboards. Although the hierarchical keyboard was specifically designed for individuals with upper limb disabilities, it performed less effectively due to its limited number of buttons, which led to slower typing speeds. Despite these limitations, the proposed hierarchical system shows promise as an intermediate solution, offering better performance than the multilevel selection method, though it still requires further refinement to reach the efficiency level of the T9 keyboard. These findings highlight the trade-off between accessibility and performance, emphasizing the importance of continued development to optimize the proposed system for users with disabilities while maintaining competitive typing efficiency.

articleTitle: Design of Wearable Device as a Fatigue Detector in Sports Activities Based on the Internet of Things
abstract: Exercise is crucial for a healthy lifestyle, but excessive fatigue can negatively impact health and performance. Detecting fatigue signals can protect against injury and improve exercise intensity. A wearable device using the MAX30102 sensor provides real-time heart rate monitoring through a smartphone application. It alerts users when fatigue is detected, calculates THRMax using the Karvonen Method, and warns if BPM readings exceed a set threshold. The MAX30102 is reliable in detecting fatigue wearables, with a small margin of error of 1.06%-6.81% compared to a conventional pulse oximeter. Data sent to Google Sheets was successfully transmitted at 100<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, with slight delays in the sending interval. The device maintains low error margins, accurately detecting THRMax and fatigue alerts, and can achieve a good success rate during running. This study confirms the practical applicability of IoT -based wearable technology in real-life exercise monitoring, correct fatigue detection, and timely feedback for optimizing and ensuring athletic performance safety.

articleTitle: Edge AI-Driven Video Analytics: A Mobile Deep Learning Framework for Victim Detection in SAR Robotics
abstract: In post-disaster search and rescue (SAR) missions, it is crucial for robots to distinguish between actual victims and dummy objects, despite their similar characteristics. Edge video analytics have demonstrated exceptional performance in such missions, however, the trade-off between high-performing deep learning models and computational complexity often results in inadequate computational efficiency for SAR robotics. This study tackles this challenge by deploying a deep learning (DL) algorithm, i.e., MobileNet Single Shot Detector (SSD), specifically tailored for embedded systems, to perform object detection and classification tasks on lab-scale SAR robots. The proposed algorithm is developed in Python and implemented on a low-powered edge computing device. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in object localization is highlighted by its mAP score of 0.6247 and an average IoU of 0.9036. Experimental tests using a confusion matrix showed that the model accurately predicted 42 dummy objects and 43 victim dolls. The model achieved an overall accuracy of 89.47%, with a precision of 1.0, a recall of 0.8947, and an F1 Score of 0.9444. Real-time testing confirmed the model's robust performance, maintaining high accuracy and a stable frame rate of 47 FPS. These findings corroborate the efficacy of the MobileNet SSD algorithm in reliably detecting and differentiating objects within embedded SAR robotic operations.
